question: In which year did the sepoy revolt take place in Vellore?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1806 CE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Sepoy Mutiny or Revolt in Vellore took place in the year **1806**.

• This revolt is also known as the Vellore Mutiny and is considered one of the earliest instances of Indian soldiers rebelling against British rule.

• The mutiny occurred on **July 10, 1806**, at Vellore, which is in the present-day Tamil Nadu.

• The primary cause of the revolt was the new dress code introduced by the British, which was seen as an affront to the religious sentiments of the Indian soldiers (sepoys).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Vellore Mutiny:**

• The Vellore Mutiny was a brief but intense rebellion by Indian soldiers against the British East India Company.

• The mutiny was sparked by the enforcement of a new dress code that included changes in the turban, facial hair, and jewelry, which were considered disrespectful to the religious and cultural practices of the Hindu and Muslim soldiers.

• On the night of July 10, 1806, the sepoys rose in rebellion, killing several British officers and soldiers.

• The mutiny was suppressed within a few hours by reinforcements from nearby areas, but it served as a precursor to larger uprisings against British rule, culminating in the Revolt of 1857.

• **Causes of the Mutiny:**

• The immediate cause was the resentment over the new dress regulations that were perceived as an attempt to undermine religious practices.

• Other underlying causes included dissatisfaction with pay, poor treatment by British officers, and the overall discontent with British policies.

• **Impact of the Mutiny:**

• Although the Vellore Mutiny was quickly suppressed, it had a lasting impact on the British administration.

• The British became more cautious in their approach to Indian traditions and religious practices.

• It highlighted the potential for discontent and rebellion among the Indian soldiers, leading to changes in the management and treatment of the sepoys.
